items.title: Rejection sampling
items.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S,\mu)$ be a measure space. The nonnegative measurable
functions $\tilde f,\tilde g:S\to[0,\infty)$ are the target and proposal
shapes, with
$$Z_f:=\int_S\tilde f\,d\mu\in(0,\infty),\qquad Z_g:=\int_S\tilde g\,d\mu\in(0,\infty).$$
The normalized densities $\bar f:=\tilde f/Z_f$ and $\bar g:=\tilde g/Z_g$
are measurable by closure under scalar multiplication
([[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]]). Their
integrals are one by homogeneity of the nonnegative integral
([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Thus their
density measures are probability laws by
[[def-measure-with-density]] and [[def-probability-measure]]:
$$F(A):=Z_f^{-1}\int_A\tilde f\,d\mu,\qquad G(A):=Z_g^{-1}\int_A\tilde g\,d\mu\quad(A\in\mathcal S).$$
Assume a finite $c>0$ satisfies $\tilde f\le c\tilde g$ outside a common
$\mu$-null set. Use finite-valued representatives; values on that null set
do not affect $F$ or $G$.

The stochastic input is an ideal sequence of independent proposal draws
$Y_i$ with common law $G$ and independent auxiliary draws $U_i$ with common
law $\Lambda$, where $\Lambda$ is the uniform probability law on $(0,1)$:
$\Lambda(U\le t)=t$ for $0\le t\le1$. The two sequences are independent, so
the pairs $(Y_i,U_i)$ are IID in the sense of
[[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]. This contract
assumes exact draws; it makes no claim about a finite-precision pseudorandom
generator.

Define the measurable acceptance function
$$a(y):=\begin{cases} 0,&\tilde g(y)=0,\\ \min\!\left\{1,\dfrac{\tilde f(y)}{c\tilde g(y)}\right\},&\tilde g(y)>0. \end{cases}$$
It is measurable. The reciprocal extension $h:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$,
$h(t)=1/t$ for $t>0$ and $h(0)=0$, is Borel: for every real $r$, its strict
upper level set is $[0,\infty)$ if $r<0$, $(0,\infty)$ if $r=0$, and
$(0,1/r)$ if $r>0$. These are Borel sets in the subspace $[0,\infty)$ by
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]], so the threshold characterization
[[thm-threshold-characterisations-of-real-and-extended-real-measurability]]
applies. Equivalently,
$a(y)=\min\{1,\tilde f(y)h(\tilde g(y))/c\}$. Arithmetic operations and Borel
composition preserve measurability by
[[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]] and
[[thm-composition-with-borel-functions-preserves-measurability]]. On the
envelope set this is exactly $\tilde f(y)/(c\tilde g(y))$. If the quotient
exceeds $1$ at an exceptional point, replacing it by $1$ does not change the
test $U_i\le\tilde f(y)/(c\tilde g(y))$, since $U_i\in(0,1)$.

**Procedure.** For $i=1,2,\ldots$, draw $(Y_i,U_i)$. If $U_i\le a(Y_i)$,
return $Y_i$ and stop; otherwise continue to the next pair. When
$\tilde f=f$ and $\tilde g=g$ are normalized densities, integrating
$f\le cg$ gives $c\ge1$, and the rule is the usual threshold $f(Y_i)/(cg(Y_i))$.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 4 §4.7

items.title: Counting-measure integration is a nonnegative series
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and let $\#$ be counting measure on
$(\mathbb N,\mathcal P(\mathbb N))$ ([[def-counting-measure]],
[[prop-counting-measure-is-a-measure]]). For every measurable
$f:\mathbb N\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb N} f\,d\#=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}f(n),$$
where the right side is the nonnegative extended series of
[[def-nonnegative-extended-series]].

references.title: Measure Theory, Princeton University MAT425 Spring 2025 Lecture Notes, Example 2.42 and Claim 2.50

items.title: Rejection sampling has the target acceptance law
items.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S,\mu)$ be a measure space and let
$\tilde f,\tilde g:S\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable with
$0<Z_f:=\int\tilde f\,d\mu<\infty$ and
$0<Z_g:=\int\tilde g\,d\mu<\infty$. Suppose $c>0$ is finite and
$\tilde f\le c\tilde g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Apply
[[alg-rejection-sampling]] with proposal law
$G(A)=Z_g^{-1}\int_A\tilde g\,d\mu$. If $N$ is the first accepted proposal,
then $N<\infty$ almost surely, the per-proposal acceptance probability is
$$p=\frac{Z_f}{cZ_g},$$
and for every $A\in\mathcal S$,
$$\mathbb P(Y_N\in A)=\frac1{Z_f}\int_A\tilde f\,d\mu.$$
Thus the accepted law has density $\tilde f/Z_f$. In the normalized case
$Z_f=Z_g=1$, this gives acceptance probability $1/c$ and accepted density
$f$; necessarily $c\ge1$.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 4 §4.7

items.title: Expected proposal count under a finite rejection envelope
items.statement:
In the setup of [[thm-rejection-sampling-has-target-acceptance-law]], let $N$
be the number of proposals through and including the first accepted proposal.
With $p=Z_f/(cZ_g)$ and $q=1-p$, for every integer $k\ge1$,
$$\mathbb P(N=k)=q^{k-1}p,\qquad \mathbb E[N]=\frac1p=\frac{cZ_g}{Z_f}.$$
Thus $N$ is geometric on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$. For normalized target and proposal
densities, $\mathbb E[N]=c$.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 4 §4.7

items.title: A lighter-tailed proposal has no finite rejection envelope
items.statement:
On $\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ with counting measure, put $f(0)=g(0)=0$ and
for $n\ge1$ define
$$f(n)=\frac1{n(n+1)},\qquad g(n)=\frac4{n(n+1)(n+2)}.$$
Both are probability masses, but their ratio
$f(n)/g(n)=(n+2)/4$ for $n\ge1$ is unbounded. Thus this lighter-tailed
proposal has no finite rejection envelope for the target.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 4 §4.7

items.title: A bounded target-to-proposal density ratio
items.statement:
On $S=\{a,b\}$ with counting measure, let the target masses be
$f(a)=1/4,\ f(b)=3/4$ and the proposal masses be $g(a)=g(b)=1/2$.
The density ratio is bounded by $c=3/2$. Rejection sampling has acceptance
probability $2/3$, returns the target law, and has expected proposal count
$3/2$.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 4 §4.7

items.title: Rejection sampling with unnormalized finite masses
items.statement:
On $S=\{a,b\}$ with counting measure, take unnormalized target masses
$\tilde f(a)=2,\ \tilde f(b)=1$ and proposal shape
$\tilde g(a)=\tilde g(b)=1$. With $c=2$, the envelope holds and
$Z_f=3,\ Z_g=2$. Rejection sampling accepts with probability $3/4$, returns
normalized target masses $(2/3,1/3)$, and uses $4/3$ proposals on average.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 4 §4.7
